subproblems.title: Restriction of covectors along ι(0, ·) and contraction with e₀ do not increase the Euclidean norm
subproblems.statement: Notation: ι(t, x) := WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.cons t (WithLp.ofLp x)) ∈ ℝ^{N+1} for t ∈ ℝ, x ∈ ℝ^N; Jv := ι(0, v) = WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.cons 0 (WithLp.ofLp v)); e₀ := EuclideanSpace.single 0 1 ∈ ℝ^{N+1}; |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α; 𝒟^m(ℝ^P) := TestFormOn univ m and 𝒟_m(ℝ^P) := GeometricCurrentOn univ m (forms and currents on all of ℝ^P = Euclid P); M(T) := T.mass = T.massOn univ; spt T := T.support. Assume (L1): for all N, N', k ∈ ℕ, every continuous linear A : ℝ^N → ℝ^{N'} and every k-covector β on ℝ^{N'}, |β.compContinuousLinearMap A| ≤ ‖A‖^k·|β|; and (L2): for all N, k ∈ ℕ, v ∈ ℝ^N and every (k+1)-covector β on ℝ^N, |β.curryLeft v| ≤ ‖v‖·|β|. Then (R1) for all N, k there is a continuous linear map Φ from (k+1)-covectors on ℝ^{N+1} to k-covectors on ℝ^N with Φ(γ)(v_1, …, v_k) = γ(e₀, Jv_1, …, Jv_k) for all γ and v, and |Φ(γ)| ≤ |γ| for all γ; and (R2) for all N, k there is a continuous linear map Ψ from k-covectors on ℝ^{N+1} to k-covectors on ℝ^N with Ψ(γ)(v_1, …, v_k) = γ(Jv_1, …, Jv_k) for all γ and v, and |Ψ(γ)| ≤ |γ| for all γ.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 (pointwise bounds) of the parent proof, with the operators Φ(γ) = (γ.curryLeft e₀).compContinuousLinearMap J and Ψ(γ) = γ.compContinuousLinearMap J made explicit. Notation as in the statement.
1. J is continuous linear. Fix N. For u, v ∈ ℝ^N and a ∈ ℝ, the coordinates of J(u + v) are 0 at index 0 and u_j + v_j at index j + 1, which are the coordinates of Ju + Jv; likewise J(a·v) = a·Jv (compare coordinates, splitting the index with Fin.cases). So v ↦ Jv is ℝ-linear, and a linear map between finite-dimensional normed spaces is continuous (LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap). Call the resulting continuous linear map J : ℝ^N →L[ℝ] ℝ^{N+1}; by construction J v = WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.cons 0 (WithLp.ofLp v)).
2. ‖J‖ ≤ 1. For v ∈ ℝ^N, ‖Jv‖² = Σ_{i : Fin (N+1)} |(Jv)_i|² = |0|² + Σ_{j : Fin N} |v_j|² = ‖v‖² (EuclideanSpace.norm_eq and Fin.sum_univ_succ), so ‖Jv‖ = ‖v‖ ≤ 1·‖v‖, and ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_le_bound gives ‖J‖ ≤ 1. Since 0 ≤ ‖J‖ ≤ 1, also ‖J‖^m ≤ 1 for every m ∈ ℕ (pow_le_one₀).
3. ‖e₀‖ = ‖EuclideanSpace.single 0 1‖ = |1| = 1.
4. Proof of (R1). Fix N, k. Let Φ be the composite of three continuous linear maps: γ ↦ γ.curryLeft (the linear isometry ContinuousAlternatingMap.curryLeftLI, viewed as a continuous linear map from (k+1)-covectors on ℝ^{N+1} to ℝ^{N+1} →L[ℝ] (k-covectors on ℝ^{N+1})), evaluation at e₀ (ContinuousLinearMap.apply ℝ _ e₀), and β ↦ β.compContinuousLinearMap J (ContinuousAlternatingMap.compContinuousLinearMapCLM J). Then Φ is continuous linear and Φ(γ) = (γ.curryLeft e₀).compContinuousLinearMap J. For v ∈ (ℝ^N)^k, Φ(γ)(v) = (γ.curryLeft e₀)(J ∘ v) = γ(Matrix.vecCons e₀ (J ∘ v)) (compContinuousLinearMap_apply and curryLeft_apply_apply). The tuples Matrix.vecCons e₀ (J ∘ v) and Fin.cons e₀ (fun i => WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.cons 0 (WithLp.ofLp (v i)))) agree at index 0 (both are e₀) and at every index i + 1 (both are J(v i), by step 1), so Φ(γ)(v) = γ(e₀, Jv_1, …, Jv_k), the required formula. For the bound, (L1) with dimensions N and N + 1, degree k, A := J and β := γ.curryLeft e₀ gives |Φ(γ)| ≤ ‖J‖^k·|γ.curryLeft e₀| ≤ 1·|γ.curryLeft e₀| = |γ.curryLeft e₀|, by step 2 and |γ.curryLeft e₀| ≥ 0 (covectorEuclideanNorm_nonneg). Then (L2) with dimension N + 1, degree k, v := e₀ and β := γ gives |γ.curryLeft e₀| ≤ ‖e₀‖·|γ| = |γ| by step 3. Hence |Φ(γ)| ≤ |γ|.
5. Proof of (R2). Fix N, k. Let Ψ := ContinuousAlternatingMap.compContinuousLinearMapCLM J, a continuous linear map with Ψ(γ) = γ.compContinuousLinearMap J; so Ψ(γ)(v) = γ(J ∘ v) = γ(Jv_1, …, Jv_k) by step 1. (L1) with dimensions N and N + 1, degree k, A := J and β := γ gives |Ψ(γ)| ≤ ‖J‖^k·|γ| ≤ |γ| by step 2 and |γ| ≥ 0.
6. Steps 4 and 5 hold for all N and k, which is the conclusion (R1) ∧ (R2). □
proof_key_steps: J v := ι(0, v) is a continuous linear map ℝ^N → ℝ^{N+1} with ‖Jv‖ = ‖v‖, so ‖J‖ ≤ 1 and ‖J‖^k ≤ 1; ‖e₀‖ = 1.
Φ := compContinuousLinearMapCLM J ∘ (evaluation at e₀) ∘ curryLeftLI is continuous linear with Φ(γ)(v) = γ(e₀, Jv_1, …, Jv_k).
(L1) with A = J and (L2) with v = e₀ give |Φ(γ)| ≤ ‖J‖^k·|γ.curryLeft e₀| ≤ ‖e₀‖·|γ| = |γ|.
Ψ := compContinuousLinearMapCLM J satisfies Ψ(γ)(v) = γ(Jv) and |Ψ(γ)| ≤ ‖J‖^k·|γ| ≤ |γ| by (L1).

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 (slice operator) of the parent proof. Notation as in the statement.
1. Continuity of the integrands. Fix x ∈ ℝ^N. The map t ↦ ι(t, x) = WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.cons t (WithLp.ofLp x)) is continuous ℝ → ℝ^{N+1}: its coordinates are t and the constants x_j (in Lean, fun_prop proves it). Every ω ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^{N+1}) is smooth (its membership proof contains ContDiff ℝ ∞ ω), hence continuous, and for a fixed tuple w evaluation γ ↦ γ(w) is continuous on covectors (continuous_eval_const). Hence g_{ω,x,w}(t) := ω(ι(t, x))(w) is continuous in t and therefore interval integrable on [0, 1] (Continuous.intervalIntegrable).
2. Choice. Fix N, k. By (SA), choose for every ω ∈ 𝒟^{k+1}(ℝ^{N+1}) a test form η_ω ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^N) with (F_ω): η_ω(x)(v) = ∫_0^1 ω(ι(t, x))(e₀, Jv_1, …, Jv_k) dt for all x, v, and with tsupport η_ω ⊆ {x : ∃ t ∈ [0, 1], ι(t, x) ∈ tsupport ω}.
3. Uniqueness. If θ ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^N) satisfies (F_ω) for all x and v, then θ = η_ω: for every x the covectors θ(x) and η_ω(x) take the same value (the same integral) on every tuple v, so θ(x) = η_ω(x) (ContinuousAlternatingMap.ext); thus the underlying forms coincide and the test forms are equal (Subtype.ext).
4. Linearity. Define S(ω) := η_ω. (a) Additivity: for ω₁, ω₂ and all x, v, (η_{ω₁} + η_{ω₂})(x)(v) = η_{ω₁}(x)(v) + η_{ω₂}(x)(v) = ∫_0^1 ω₁(ι(t, x))(e₀, Jv) dt + ∫_0^1 ω₂(ι(t, x))(e₀, Jv) dt = ∫_0^1 (ω₁(ι(t, x))(e₀, Jv) + ω₂(ι(t, x))(e₀, Jv)) dt (intervalIntegral.integral_add; both integrands are interval integrable by step 1) = ∫_0^1 (ω₁ + ω₂)(ι(t, x))(e₀, Jv) dt, because test forms and covectors are added pointwise. So η_{ω₁} + η_{ω₂} satisfies (F_{ω₁+ω₂}), and step 3 gives S(ω₁ + ω₂) = S(ω₁) + S(ω₂). (b) Homogeneity: for a ∈ ℝ, (a·η_ω)(x)(v) = a·∫_0^1 ω(ι(t, x))(e₀, Jv) dt = ∫_0^1 a·ω(ι(t, x))(e₀, Jv) dt (intervalIntegral.integral_const_mul) = ∫_0^1 (a·ω)(ι(t, x))(e₀, Jv) dt, so step 3 gives S(a·ω) = a·S(ω). Hence S is an ℝ-linear map 𝒟^{k+1}(ℝ^{N+1}) → 𝒟^k(ℝ^N).
5. Properties (i) and (ii) are the formula (F_ω) and the support inclusion chosen in step 2.
6. Property (iii). Let ω ∈ 𝒟^{k+1}(ℝ^{N+1}) and c ∈ ℝ satisfy |ω(y)| ≤ c for all y, and fix x ∈ ℝ^N. Take Φ from (R1) for (N, k) and put f(t) := Φ(ω(ι(t, x))) for t ∈ ℝ. f is continuous, being the composite of the continuous linear Φ, the continuous ω and the continuous t ↦ ι(t, x) (step 1). For every v, by (i) and the formula for Φ, S(ω)(x)(v) = ∫_0^1 ω(ι(t, x))(e₀, Jv_1, …, Jv_k) dt = ∫_0^1 Φ(ω(ι(t, x)))(v) dt = ∫_0^1 f(t)(v) dt (the integrands agree pointwise). For every t, in particular t ∈ [0, 1], |f(t)| ≤ |ω(ι(t, x))| ≤ c by the bound in (R1) and the hypothesis. So (SE) with dimension N, degree k, α := S(ω)(x), this f and this c gives |S(ω)(x)| ≤ c.
7. Steps 2–6 work for every N and k, which proves the statement. □
proof_key_steps: t ↦ ω(ι(t, x))(w) is continuous (ω smooth, ι(·, x) continuous, evaluation continuous), hence interval integrable on [0, 1].
Choose η_ω from (SA); any test form satisfying the slice formula of ω equals η_ω (ContinuousAlternatingMap.ext, Subtype.ext).
S(ω) := η_ω is additive and homogeneous by uniqueness and linearity of interval integrals; (i), (ii) hold by the choice.
(iii): apply (SE) to α = S(ω)(x) and f(t) = Φ(ω(ι(t, x))), continuous with |f(t)| ≤ |ω(ι(t, x))| ≤ c by (R1).

subproblems.title: Cylinder current X ↦ X ∘ S from the bounded-current constructor, with mass bound and additivity
subproblems.statement: Notation: ι(t, x) := WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.cons t (WithLp.ofLp x)) ∈ ℝ^{N+1} for t ∈ ℝ, x ∈ ℝ^N; Jv := ι(0, v) = WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.cons 0 (WithLp.ofLp v)); e₀ := EuclideanSpace.single 0 1 ∈ ℝ^{N+1}; |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α; 𝒟^m(ℝ^P) := TestFormOn univ m and 𝒟_m(ℝ^P) := GeometricCurrentOn univ m (forms and currents on all of ℝ^P = Euclid P); M(T) := T.mass = T.massOn univ; spt T := T.support. Assume (MSB): for all N, k ∈ ℕ, X ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^N) with M(X) < ∞, ψ ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^N) and c ∈ ℝ with |ψ(x)| ≤ c for every x ∈ spt X, one has |X(ψ)| ≤ c·M(X).toReal; and (BC): for all N, k ∈ ℕ, every ℝ-linear T₀ : 𝒟^k(ℝ^N) → ℝ and C ∈ ℝ such that |T₀(ω)| ≤ C·c whenever ω ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^N), c ∈ ℝ and |ω(x)| ≤ c for all x, there is T ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^N) with T(ω) = T₀(ω) for all ω and M(T) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal C. Then for all N, k ∈ ℕ and every ℝ-linear S : 𝒟^{k+1}(ℝ^{N+1}) → 𝒟^k(ℝ^N) satisfying (iii) [for every ω and c ∈ ℝ with |ω(y)| ≤ c for all y ∈ ℝ^{N+1}, |S(ω)(x)| ≤ c for all x ∈ ℝ^N], there is a map cyl : 𝒟_k(ℝ^N) → 𝒟_{k+1}(ℝ^{N+1}) such that (a) for every X with M(X) < ∞: cyl(X)(ω) = X(S(ω)) for all ω ∈ 𝒟^{k+1}(ℝ^{N+1}) and M(cyl(X)) ≤ M(X); (b) cyl(X − Y) = cyl(X) − cyl(Y) for all X, Y ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^N) with M(X) < ∞ and M(Y) < ∞ (X − Y is the difference of currents of the frozen contract).
subproblems.lean_statement: (∀ (N k : ℕ) (X : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid N)) k) (ψ : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid N)) k) (c : ℝ), X.mass < ∞ → (∀ x ∈ X.support, covectorEuclideanNorm ((ψ : DifferentialForm (Euclid N) k) x) ≤ c) → |X ψ| ≤ c * X.mass.toReal) → (∀ (N k : ℕ) (T₀ : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid N)) k →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ) (C : ℝ), (∀ (ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid N)) k) (c : ℝ), (∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid N) k) x) ≤ c) → |T₀ ω| ≤ C * c) → ∃ T : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid N)) k, (∀ ω, T ω = T₀ ω) ∧ T.mass ≤ ENNReal.ofReal C) → ∀ (N k : ℕ) (S : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid (N + 1))) (k + 1) →ₗ[ℝ] TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid N)) k), (∀ (ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid (N + 1))) (k + 1)) (c : ℝ), (∀ y : Euclid (N + 1), covectorEuclideanNorm ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid (N + 1)) (k + 1)) y) ≤ c) → ∀ x : Euclid N, covectorEuclideanNorm ((S ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid N) k) x) ≤ c) → ∃ cyl : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid N)) k → GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid (N + 1))) (k + 1), (∀ X : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid N)) k, X.mass < ∞ → (∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid (N + 1))) (k + 1), cyl X ω = X (S ω)) ∧ (cyl X).mass ≤ X.mass) ∧ ∀ X Y : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid N)) k, X.mass < ∞ → Y.mass < ∞ → cyl (X - Y) = cyl X - cyl Y
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 3, 5 and 6 of the parent proof. Fix N, k and a linear S with property (iii).
1. The bounded functional. Let X ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^N) with M(X) < ∞, and let T₀ := X.toCurrent ∘ S, i.e. T₀(ω) = X(S(ω)); T₀ is ℝ-linear as a composite of linear maps. Let ω ∈ 𝒟^{k+1}(ℝ^{N+1}) and c ∈ ℝ with |ω(y)| ≤ c for all y. By (iii), |S(ω)(x)| ≤ c for all x ∈ ℝ^N, in particular for all x ∈ spt X, so (MSB) with dimension N, degree k and ψ := S(ω) gives |T₀(ω)| = |X(S(ω))| ≤ c·M(X).toReal = M(X).toReal·c.
2. Construction. By (BC) in dimension N + 1 and degree k + 1, applied to T₀ and C := M(X).toReal, there is T_X ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(ℝ^{N+1}) with T_X(ω) = X(S(ω)) for all ω and M(T_X) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(M(X).toReal) = M(X) (ENNReal.ofReal_toReal, since M(X) ≠ ∞).
3. Definition of cyl. Using classical choice, put cyl(X) := T_X (the current chosen in step 2) if M(X) < ∞, and cyl(X) := 0 otherwise. Then for every X with M(X) < ∞ we have cyl(X)(ω) = X(S(ω)) for all ω and M(cyl(X)) ≤ M(X). This is (a).
4. Finite mass of differences. Let M(X) < ∞ and M(Y) < ∞. By definition, M(X − Y) is the supremum of ENNReal.ofReal((X − Y)(ω)) over the admissible ω ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^N), i.e. tsupport ω ⊆ univ and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x. For such ω, (X − Y)(ω) = X(ω) − Y(ω) (the difference of currents acts by the difference of the underlying linear functionals), and (MSB) with c = 1 gives |X(ω)| ≤ M(X).toReal and |Y(ω)| ≤ M(Y).toReal. Hence ENNReal.ofReal((X − Y)(ω)) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(M(X).toReal + M(Y).toReal), and taking the supremum (sSup_le), M(X − Y) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(M(X).toReal + M(Y).toReal) < ∞ (ENNReal.ofReal_lt_top). This is the parent's bound M(X − Y) ≤ M(X) + M(Y), obtained here through (MSB).
5. Additivity (b). Let M(X) < ∞ and M(Y) < ∞. By step 4, (a) applies to X − Y as well as to X and Y. So for every ω, cyl(X − Y)(ω) = (X − Y)(S(ω)) = X(S(ω)) − Y(S(ω)) = cyl(X)(ω) − cyl(Y)(ω) = (cyl(X) − cyl(Y))(ω). Two currents with the same value on every test form are equal (GeometricCurrentOn.ext), so cyl(X − Y) = cyl(X) − cyl(Y). □
proof_key_steps: For M(X) < ∞, T₀ := X ∘ S is linear and |T₀(ω)| ≤ M(X).toReal·c whenever |ω| ≤ c, by (iii) and (MSB).
(BC) yields T_X with T_X(ω) = X(S(ω)) and M(T_X) ≤ ofReal(M(X).toReal) = M(X).
cyl(X) := T_X if M(X) < ∞, else 0; this gives (a).
M(X − Y) < ∞ by (MSB) with c = 1 on admissible forms; then cyl(X − Y) = cyl(X) − cyl(Y) by evaluation on every ω and GeometricCurrentOn.ext.

subproblems.title: Support of a slice-composed current lies in ι([0, 1] × spt X) and is compact
subproblems.statement: Notation: ι(t, x) := WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.cons t (WithLp.ofLp x)) ∈ ℝ^{N+1} for t ∈ ℝ, x ∈ ℝ^N; Jv := ι(0, v) = WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.cons 0 (WithLp.ofLp v)); e₀ := EuclideanSpace.single 0 1 ∈ ℝ^{N+1}; |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α; 𝒟^m(ℝ^P) := TestFormOn univ m and 𝒟_m(ℝ^P) := GeometricCurrentOn univ m (forms and currents on all of ℝ^P = Euclid P); M(T) := T.mass = T.massOn univ; spt T := T.support. Assume (VO): for all P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P, S ∈ GeometricCurrentOn U n and ω ∈ TestFormOn U n with tsupport ω disjoint from spt S, S(ω) = 0. Let N, k ∈ ℕ, X ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^N) with spt X compact, Z ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(ℝ^{N+1}), and let S : 𝒟^{k+1}(ℝ^{N+1}) → 𝒟^k(ℝ^N) be any map such that tsupport S(ω) ⊆ {x ∈ ℝ^N : ∃ t ∈ [0, 1], ι(t, x) ∈ tsupport ω} for every ω, and Z(ω) = X(S(ω)) for every ω. Then spt Z is compact and spt Z ⊆ {ι(t, x) : t ∈ [0, 1], x ∈ spt X}.
subproblems.lean_statement: (∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (S : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (ω : TestFormOn U n), Disjoint (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n)) S.support → S ω = 0) → ∀ (N k : ℕ) (X : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid N)) k) (Z : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid (N + 1))) (k + 1)) (S : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid (N + 1))) (k + 1) → TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid N)) k), IsCompact X.support → (∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid (N + 1))) (k + 1), tsupport (S ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid N) k) ⊆ {x : Euclid N | ∃ t ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, (WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.cons t (WithLp.ofLp x)) : Euclid (N + 1)) ∈ tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid (N + 1)) (k + 1))}) → (∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid (N + 1))) (k + 1), Z ω = X (S ω)) → IsCompact Z.support ∧ Z.support ⊆ {y : Euclid (N + 1) | ∃ t ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, ∃ x ∈ X.support, y = WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.cons t (WithLp.ofLp x))}
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 7 of the parent proof. Let C := {ι(t, x) : t ∈ [0, 1], x ∈ spt X} ⊆ ℝ^{N+1}.
1. C is compact. C is the image of [0, 1] × spt X under (t, x) ↦ ι(t, x) = WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.cons t (WithLp.ofLp x)), which is continuous on ℝ × ℝ^N (fun_prop). [0, 1] and spt X are compact, so their product is compact (isCompact_Icc.prod) and so is its continuous image (IsCompact.image). In particular C is closed (compact sets in the Hausdorff space ℝ^{N+1} are closed), so Cᶜ is open.
2. spt Z ⊆ C. Let y ∈ spt Z and suppose y ∉ C. As Cᶜ is open, there is r > 0 with B := ball(y, r) ⊆ Cᶜ (Metric.isOpen_iff); the parent proof uses the ball of radius infDist(y, C)/2, and any ball inside Cᶜ serves. B is open; closure B ⊆ closedBall(y, r) (closure_ball_subset_closedBall), which is compact in the proper space ℝ^{N+1}, so closure B is compact (IsCompact.of_isClosed_subset); and closure B ⊆ univ. Z vanishes on B: let ω ∈ 𝒟^{k+1}(ℝ^{N+1}) with tsupport ω ⊆ B. If some x lay in tsupport S(ω) ∩ spt X, the hypothesis on S would give t ∈ [0, 1] with ι(t, x) ∈ tsupport ω ⊆ B ⊆ Cᶜ, whereas ι(t, x) ∈ C because t ∈ [0, 1] and x ∈ spt X; contradiction. So tsupport S(ω) is disjoint from spt X, and (VO) with P := N, n := k, U := univ, the current X and the test form S(ω) gives X(S(ω)) = 0; hence Z(ω) = X(S(ω)) = 0. [The parent proof reaches X(S(ω)) = 0 through the locality property and X(0) = 0; (VO) gives it directly.] Thus B is an open set with compact closure contained in univ on which Z vanishes, so B is one of the sets whose union is zeroRegion Z, and y ∈ B ⊆ zeroRegion Z. This contradicts y ∈ spt Z = univ \ zeroRegion Z. Hence spt Z ⊆ C.
3. spt Z is compact. spt Z = univ \ zeroRegion Z = (zeroRegion Z)ᶜ is closed, because zeroRegion Z is open (GeometricCurrentOn.isOpen_zeroRegion). A closed subset of the compact set C is compact (IsCompact.of_isClosed_subset), so spt Z is compact. With step 2 this proves both claims. □
proof_key_steps: C = ι([0, 1] × spt X) is a continuous image of a compact set, hence compact and closed.
For y ∉ C choose ball(y, r) ⊆ Cᶜ; it is open with compact closure.
If tsupport ω ⊆ ball(y, r), then tsupport S(ω) misses spt X, so (VO) gives Z(ω) = X(S(ω)) = 0; hence y ∈ zeroRegion Z and y ∉ spt Z.
spt Z = (zeroRegion Z)ᶜ is closed and contained in the compact C, hence compact.

subproblems.title: Finite boundary mass of a slice-composed current via the slice homotopy identities
subproblems.statement: Notation: ι(t, x) := WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.cons t (WithLp.ofLp x)) ∈ ℝ^{N+1} for t ∈ ℝ, x ∈ ℝ^N; Jv := ι(0, v) = WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.cons 0 (WithLp.ofLp v)); e₀ := EuclideanSpace.single 0 1 ∈ ℝ^{N+1}; |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α; 𝒟^m(ℝ^P) := TestFormOn univ m and 𝒟_m(ℝ^P) := GeometricCurrentOn univ m (forms and currents on all of ℝ^P = Euclid P); M(T) := T.mass = T.massOn univ; spt T := T.support. d := exteriorDerivative. Assume (MSB): for all N, k ∈ ℕ, X ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^N) with M(X) < ∞, ψ ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^N) and c ∈ ℝ with |ψ(x)| ≤ c for every x ∈ spt X, |X(ψ)| ≤ c·M(X).toReal; (SLB): for all N, k ∈ ℕ, s ∈ ℝ and ω ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^{N+1}) there is ρ ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^N) with ρ(x)(v_1, …, v_k) = ω(ι(s, x))(Jv_1, …, Jv_k) for all x, v; (SLC): for all N, k ∈ ℕ, β ∈ 𝒟^{k+1}(ℝ^{N+1}) and θ ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^N) with θ(x)(v) = ∫_0^1 β(ι(t, x))(e₀, Jv_1, …, Jv_k) dt for all x and v ∈ (ℝ^N)^k, one has for all x and v = (v_0, …, v_k) ∈ (ℝ^N)^{k+1}: ∫_0^1 dβ(ι(t, x))(e₀, Jv_0, …, Jv_k) dt = β(ι(1, x))(Jv_0, …, Jv_k) − β(ι(0, x))(Jv_0, …, Jv_k) − dθ(x)(v); (SLD): for all N, β ∈ 𝒟^0(ℝ^{N+1}), x ∈ ℝ^N and the empty tuple v: ∫_0^1 dβ(ι(t, x))(e₀) dt = β(ι(1, x))() − β(ι(0, x))(); (R2): for all N, k there is a continuous linear map Ψ from k-covectors on ℝ^{N+1} to k-covectors on ℝ^N with Ψ(γ)(v_1, …, v_k) = γ(Jv_1, …, Jv_k) and |Ψ(γ)| ≤ |γ|. Let N, k ∈ ℕ, X ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^N) with M(X) < ∞ and boundaryMassOn X univ < ∞ (that is, M(∂X) < ∞ when k ≥ 1; it is 0 when k = 0), Z ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(ℝ^{N+1}), and maps S_m : 𝒟^{m+1}(ℝ^{N+1}) → 𝒟^m(ℝ^N) (m ∈ ℕ) such that for every m: S_m(ω)(x)(v_1, …, v_m) = ∫_0^1 ω(ι(t, x))(e₀, Jv_1, …, Jv_m) dt for all ω, x, v, and |S_m(ω)(x)| ≤ c for all x whenever c ∈ ℝ and |ω(y)| ≤ c for all y. If Z(ω) = X(S_k(ω)) for all ω ∈ 𝒟^{k+1}(ℝ^{N+1}), then M(∂Z) < ∞.

(β : DifferentialForm (Euclid (N + 1)) 0) (WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.cons 0 (WithLp.ofLp x))) (fun i => WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.cons 0 (WithLp.ofLp (v i))))) → (∀ N k : ℕ, ∃ Ψ : Covector (Euclid (N + 1)) k →L[ℝ] Covector (Euclid N) k, (∀ (γ : Covector (Euclid (N + 1)) k) (v : Fin k → Euclid N), Ψ γ v = γ (fun i => WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.cons 0 (WithLp.ofLp (v i))))) ∧ ∀ γ : Covector (Euclid (N + 1)) k, covectorEuclideanNorm (Ψ γ) ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm γ) → ∀ (N k : ℕ) (X : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid N)) k) (Z : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid (N + 1))) (k + 1)) (S : ∀ m : ℕ, TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid (N + 1))) (m + 1) → TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid N)) m), X.mass < ∞ → boundaryMassOn X univ < ∞ → (∀ (m : ℕ) (ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid (N + 1))) (m + 1)) (x : Euclid N) (v : Fin m → Euclid N), (S m ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid N) m) x v = ∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..1, (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid (N + 1)) (m + 1)) (WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.cons t (WithLp.ofLp x))) (Fin.cons (EuclideanSpace.single 0 1) (fun i => WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.cons 0 (WithLp.ofLp (v i)))))) → (∀ (m : ℕ) (ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid (N + 1))) (m + 1)) (c : ℝ), (∀ y : Euclid (N + 1), covectorEuclideanNorm ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid (N + 1)) (m + 1)) y) ≤ c) → ∀ x : Euclid N, covectorEuclideanNorm ((S m ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid N) m) x) ≤ c) → (∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid (N + 1))) (k + 1), Z ω = X (S k ω)) → Z.boundary.mass < ∞
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 8 of the parent proof. Let B := 2·M(X).toReal + (boundaryMassOn X univ).toReal. M(∂Z) = M_univ(∂Z) is the supremum of ENNReal.ofReal(∂Z(ω)) over the admissible ω, namely ω ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^{N+1}) with tsupport ω ⊆ univ and |ω(y)| ≤ 1 for all y. Fix such an ω.
1. Boundary value. ∂Z(ω) = Z(dω) (GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply), where dω := exteriorDerivativeTestOn univ k ω ∈ 𝒟^{k+1}(ℝ^{N+1}) has underlying form exteriorDerivative ω. By the hypothesis on Z, ∂Z(ω) = X(S_k(dω)).
2. The end slices. For s ∈ {0, 1}, (SLB) with dimension N, degree k, this s and ω gives ρ_s ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^N) with ρ_s(x)(v) = ω(ι(s, x))(Jv_1, …, Jv_k) for all x, v. Take Ψ from (R2) for (N, k). For each x, the covectors ρ_s(x) and Ψ(ω(ι(s, x))) agree on every tuple v (both equal ω(ι(s, x))(Jv_1, …, Jv_k)), so they are equal (ContinuousAlternatingMap.ext), and |ρ_s(x)| = |Ψ(ω(ι(s, x)))| ≤ |ω(ι(s, x))| ≤ 1. As this holds at every x, in particular on spt X, (MSB) with c = 1 gives |X(ρ_s)| ≤ M(X).toReal for s = 0 and s = 1.
3. Case k = 0. Here ω ∈ 𝒟^0(ℝ^{N+1}). For every x and the empty tuple v, the slice formula for S_0 applied to dω gives S_0(dω)(x)(v) = ∫_0^1 dω(ι(t, x))(e₀) dt, and (SLD) with β := ω turns this into ω(ι(1, x))() − ω(ι(0, x))() = ρ₁(x)(v) − ρ₀(x)(v). Hence S_0(dω) = ρ₁ − ρ₀ (equal values at every x and v; ContinuousAlternatingMap.ext and Subtype.ext). By linearity of X, ∂Z(ω) = X(ρ₁ − ρ₀) = X(ρ₁) − X(ρ₀) ≤ |X(ρ₁)| + |X(ρ₀)| ≤ 2·M(X).toReal ≤ B, since (boundaryMassOn X univ).toReal ≥ 0.
4. Case k = k' + 1. Here ω ∈ 𝒟^{k'+1}(ℝ^{N+1}). Put θ := S_{k'}(ω) ∈ 𝒟^{k'}(ℝ^N). By the slice formula for S_{k'}, θ(x)(v) = ∫_0^1 ω(ι(t, x))(e₀, Jv_1, …, Jv_{k'}) dt for all x and v ∈ (ℝ^N)^{k'}, which is exactly the hypothesis of (SLC) with degree k', β := ω and this θ. So for all x and v ∈ (ℝ^N)^{k'+1}, using the slice formula for S_{k'+1} applied to dω and then (SLC): S_{k'+1}(dω)(x)(v) = ∫_0^1 dω(ι(t, x))(e₀, Jv_0, …, Jv_{k'}) dt = ω(ι(1, x))(Jv) − ω(ι(0, x))(Jv) − dθ(x)(v) = (ρ₁ − ρ₀ − dθ)(x)(v), where dθ := exteriorDerivativeTestOn univ k' θ. Therefore S_{k'+1}(dω) = ρ₁ − ρ₀ − dθ, and by linearity of X, ∂Z(ω) = X(ρ₁) − X(ρ₀) − X(dθ), where X(dθ) = ∂X(θ) by the definition of the boundary. The bound hypothesis on S_{k'} with c = 1 (|ω(y)| ≤ 1 for all y) gives |θ(x)| ≤ 1 for all x. In positive degree boundaryMassOn X univ is by definition M_univ(∂X) = M(∂X), which is finite by hypothesis, so (MSB) for the current ∂X ∈ 𝒟_{k'}(ℝ^N), ψ := θ and c = 1 gives |∂X(θ)| ≤ M(∂X).toReal = (boundaryMassOn X univ).toReal. Hence ∂Z(ω) ≤ |X(ρ₁)| + |X(ρ₀)| + |∂X(θ)| ≤ B.
5. Conclusion. In both cases ∂Z(ω) ≤ B for every admissible ω, so ENNReal.ofReal(∂Z(ω)) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(B) (ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal). Taking the supremum (sSup_le), M(∂Z) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(B) < ∞ (ENNReal.ofReal_lt_top). □
